html:
In 1565 a large Ottoman fleet and army besieged Malta for nearly four months. The Knights and the Maltese held out until a relief force from Sicily arrived in September, and the Ottomans sailed away.

Sultan Suleiman wanted Malta as a base for attacks on Italy and Spain. The Turks took Fort St Elmo after a month of fighting, but lost thousands of men there. The forts of Birgu and Senglea, defended by the Grand Master Jean de la Valette, never fell.

The siege made La Valette a hero across Catholic Europe. It halted the Ottomans in the western Mediterranean six years before the Battle of Lepanto. The knights then built a new fortified capital, Valletta, named after him. See Malta.
